title: Stop roaming where the One is already near
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 256
summary: The pauree begins by challenging the wandering search directly and turning the seeker inward. It then sends the heart into Saadh Sangat, where ego is torn down and peace becomes possible.
whyItMatters: This one meets the person exhausted by spiritual roaming, method-switching, or lonely searching. Kept near, it makes company and inward turning feel more trustworthy than the next forest.
takeaway: Let this stay with you: search inwardly and let Sangat tear down the proud mound.

lines.gurmukhi: ਢਢਾ ਢੂਢਤ ਕਹ ਫਿਰਹੁ ਢੂਢਨੁ ਇਆ ਮਨ ਮਾਹਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: ddaddaa ddooddat keh firahu ddooddan iaa man maeh ||
lines.translation: DHADHA: Where are you going, wandering and searching? Search instead within your own mind.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸੰਗਿ ਤੁਹਾਰੈ ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਬਸੈ ਬਨੁ ਬਨੁ ਕਹਾ ਫਿਰਾਹਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: sa(n)g tuhaarai prabh basai ban ban kahaa firaeh ||
lines.translation: God is with you, so why do you wander around from forest to forest?
In the Saadh Sangat, the Company of the Holy, tear down the mound of your frightful, egotistical pride.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸੁਖੁ ਪਾਵਹੁ ਸਹਜੇ ਬਸਹੁ ਦਰਸਨੁ ਦੇਖਿ ਨਿਹਾਲ ॥
lines.transliteration: sukh paavahu sahaje basahu dharasan dhekh nihaal ||
lines.translation: You shall find peace, and abide in intuitive bliss; gazing upon the Blessed Vision of God's Darshan, you shall be delighted.

lines.gurmukhi: ਢੇਰੀ ਜਾਮੈ ਜਮਿ ਮਰੈ ਗਰਭ ਜੋਨਿ ਦੁਖ ਪਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: dderee jaamai jam marai garabh jon dhukh pai ||
lines.translation: One who has such a mound as this, dies and suffers the pain of reincarnation through the womb.

lines.gurmukhi: ਮੋਹ ਮਗਨ ਲਪਟਤ ਰਹੈ ਹਉ ਹਉ ਆਵੈ ਜਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: moh magan lapaTat rahai hau hau aavai jai ||
lines.translation: One who is intoxicated by emotional attachment, entangled in egotism, selfishness and conceit, shall continue coming and going in reincarnation.

lines.gurmukhi: ਢਹਤ ਢਹਤ ਅਬ ਢਹਿ ਪਰੇ ਸਾਧ ਜਨਾ ਸਰਨਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: ddahat ddahat ab ddeh pare saadh janaa saranai ||
lines.translation: Slowly and steadily, I have now surrendered to the Holy Saints; I have come to their Sanctuary.

lines.gurmukhi: ਦੁਖ ਕੇ ਫਾਹੇ ਕਾਟਿਆ ਨਾਨਕ ਲੀਏ ਸਮਾਇ ॥੩੦॥
lines.transliteration: dhukh ke faahe kaaTiaa naanak le'ee samai ||30||
lines.translation: God has cut away the noose of my pain; O Nanak, He has merged me into Himself. ||30||

structure: First, it begins by confronting wandering instead of admiring it.
Then, it turns the seeker toward inner search and the company of the holy.
Finally, it ends by linking peace and delight to the breaking of egotistical pride.
